newsitem.title: UK: BAA passenger traffic up 3.2 pct in Sept.
newsitem.headline: BAA passenger traffic up 3.2 pct in Sept.

text.p: BAA Plc, the British airport operator, said on Thursday its seven UK airports handled a total of 9.4 million passengers in September -- a rise of 3.2 percent on the same month last year.
BAA said the number of air transport movements rose by 5.4 percent and the total air cargo tonnage handled rose by 5.5 percent to 121,962 tonnes compared with the same month last year.
Most major markets recorded healthy growth, with traffic in the UK domestic and Irish markets both increasing by eight percent and the European scheduled market growing five percent.
Traffic on North Atlantic routes increased by 2.6 percent and other long haul traffic rose 6.8 percent.
But BBA said a continuing trend in the European charter market showed an eight percent fall on the same month last year.
Among individual airports, Stansted in Essex, near London, recorded a two percent rise and Edinburgh, Scotland, a hefty 16 percent rise.

London's Gatwick recorded an overall five percent increase -- despite an eight percent drop in its charter traffic -- and Heathrow saw one percent more passengers than last September, BAA said in a statement.
